newsitem.title: CANADA: Noranda Inc sees better margins in '97.
newsitem.headline: Noranda Inc sees better margins in '97.

text.p: Canada's Noranda Inc said on Friday lower costs and improving prices are expected to deliver better margins for the balance of 1997.
Noranda chief executive officer David Kerr said the company's outlook for the year is cautiously optimistic.

"Looking ahead to the balance of the year, we expect better margins resulting from lower costs and improvements in realized prices for zinc, aluminum, newsprint, papers, oil and natural gas," Kerr said in a statement.
Noranda on Friday reported net income of C$61 million in the second quarter ended June 30, down from C$66 million in the same period a year ago.
Over six months, earnings fell to C$120 million from C$167 in the first half of 1996.
Kerr said prices for metals and forest products were generally lower in the first six months of 1997 than for the same period in 1996.
The company said its Noranda Forest unit is preparing for the implementation phase of its margin improvement program.

"It is expected that this company-wide initiative will result in an annualized increase in operating profit in excess of C$100 million by the end of 1998. This is to be achieved through improvements to product mix, customer mix, increased volumes and reduced costs," Noranda said.
